properties.name: THE REFRAME — it was never one strange server. TWO live agent sessions sit at 476 and 945 MB; FIVE controlled reconstructions cap at 101-178. The only unvaried variable is duration and session churn
properties.statement:
ESTABLISHED 2026-09-13 jointly by the reflow2 and flo2 sessions, after the survey that produced fact:an-orphaned-serve-shared-daemon-holds-the-store-and-475mb-2026-09-13 was corrected. That correction removed a false orphan AND changed the shape of the whole investigation, which is why this is recorded separately.

    LIVE AGENT SESSIONS (long-running, real MCP client, repeated reconnects)
        flo2's daemon        202 nodes, 2.9 MB export, 3.4 h      476 MB
        reflow2's daemon   4,403 nodes, 14.7 MB export, 0.9 h     945 MB

    CONTROLLED RECONSTRUCTIONS (fresh server, ~5 minutes, ONE session, curl or one held connection)
        arm H  140 identical reads, tiny payloads                 101 MB
        arm P  128 mixed calls, 17 KB payloads each               158 MB
        arm M  128 mixed calls, tiny payloads                     173 MB
        arm K  128 mixed calls, ONE held connection               178 MB

⭐ FLO2'S SERVER WAS NEVER THE OUTLIER. Set beside reflow2's own live daemon it is the SMALLER of the two, and the ordering runs the way design size predicts — 202 nodes at 476 MB, 4,403 nodes at 945 MB. What is anomalous is not one server; it is that BOTH LIVE SESSIONS SIT ABOVE A BAND THAT FIVE RECONSTRUCTIONS CANNOT LEAVE. That is a far narrower finding and a far more testable one.

WHAT HAS BEEN KILLED, so the remaining space is small and named: RocksDB column-family defaults, the tantivy writer heap, glibc arena count against core count (same machine, nproc 4), retention tracking call COUNT, retention tracking per-call PAYLOAD SIZE, and connection churn against a held connection. Six candidates, three from each side, every one refuted by a measurement that could have confirmed it. Arm P is the cleanest of them: 85x the bytes of arm M and LOWER resident memory.

⭐ WHAT IS LEFT IS ONE VARIABLE AND NEITHER SIDE HAS MOVED IT: DURATION, and what accumulates along it. Every arm ran about five minutes and minted exactly ONE session. The two live daemons have run 3.4 and 0.9 hours across an agent's reconnects, each reconnect minting a new session and a new seat. Seat and session state, debounced export timers, and background sweeps are all untested. THE NEXT EXPERIMENT IS AN ARM THAT RUNS FOR HOURS AND RECONNECTS REPEATEDLY, not another arm that varies what is sent.

📌 EXPORT SIZE STILL EXPLAINS PART OF IT AND MUST NOT BE DISCARDED. Five 14.7 MB exports took an arm from 140 to 433 MB, and flo2 confirms their own export cost tracks document size — their fourteen exports at 0.45 MB cost about 28 MB in total. So export retention is real and scales with the document; it accounts for much of reflow2's 945 MB and little of flo2's 476 MB. Both can be true.

WHAT IS NOT ESTABLISHED: whether duration alone reproduces the gap; whether seats or sessions accumulate without bound; whether the two live daemons would fall back to the band if their clients disconnected. No long-running arm has been taken.
